about: Formant (and fricative noise peak) reference ranges by sound and age for the Speak Up 'Hz ranges' tool. Built by T3, 2026-11-04. Read sound-book/NORMS-README.md. Values in Hz. lo/hi = mean minus and plus 1 SD unless 'spread' says otherwise. These are where typical speakers usually fall, never pass/fail lines.

hillenbrand1995.cite: Hillenbrand, J., Getty, L. A., Clark, M. J., and Wheeler, K. (1995). Acoustic characteristics of American English vowels. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 97(5), 3099-3111.
hillenbrand1995.how: Means and SDs computed by T3 from the authors' token file vowdata.dat (homepages.wmich.edu/~hillenbr/voweldata.html), steady-state F0, F1, F2, F3; zero (unmeasurable) values left out. Crossref confirms the citation.

flipsen2001.cite: Flipsen, P., Jr., Shriberg, L. D., Weismer, G., Karlsson, H. B., and McSweeny, J. L. (2001). Acoustic phenotypes for speech-genetics studies: Reference data for residual /ɝ/ distortions. Clinical Linguistics and Phonetics, 15(8), 603-630.
flipsen2001.how: Appendix (pp. 629-630), F3-F2 mean (SD) and token n by age and sex, computed from Lee et al. (1999) tokens of 'bird'. Read from the authors' PDF (web.waisman.wisc.edu/phonology/pubs/PUB20.pdf); every cell checked against the rendered page image on 2026-11-04.

lee1999.cite: Lee, S., Potamianos, A., and Narayanan, S. (1999). Acoustics of children's speech: Developmental changes of temporal and spectral parameters. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 105(3), 1455-1468.
lee1999.how: Citation confirmed on Crossref. The raw per-age F1/F2/F3 values are behind the publisher's bot check and were not read; only the F3-F2 values derived from its tokens (flipsen2001) are used.

mcallisterbyun2012.cite: McAllister Byun, T., and Hitchcock, E. R. (2012). Investigating the use of traditional and spectral biofeedback approaches to intervention for /r/ misarticulation. American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology, 21(3), 207-221.
mcallisterbyun2012.how: Table 3, F3 mean (SD) of /r/ productions rated correct by at least 2 of 3 certified SLPs, by context; 11 children aged 6;0 to 11;9 in treatment for /r/ errors. Read from the full text.

wong2025.cite: Wong, E., and Munson, B. (2025). Beyond spectral moments: Validating alternative measures of sibilant fricatives using listener ratings of children's speech. JASA Express Letters, 5(10), 105202.
wong2025.how: Table 2, M1 and mid-frequency peak (3-9 kHz) mean (SD) by transcription category; 63 children aged 2;6 to 3;6. Read from the PMC full text (PMC12499953).

todd2011.cite: Todd, A. E., Edwards, J. R., and Litovsky, R. Y. (2011). Production of contrast between sibilant fricatives by children with cochlear implants. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 130(6), 3969-3979.
todd2011.how: Group spectral means (no SDs given in the text) read from the PMC full text (PMC3253598). Used as reference points only, not as bands.

espywilson1992.cite: Espy-Wilson, C. Y. (1992). Acoustic measures for linguistic features distinguishing the semivowels /w j r l/ in American English. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 92(2), 736-757.
espywilson1992.how: Table VI, mean F1/F2/F3 across 4 adult speakers (2 men, 2 women), no SDs. Read from the author-hosted PDF (scl.umd.edu). Reference points only.

koenig2013.cite: Koenig, L. L., Shadle, C. H., Preston, J. L., and Mooshammer, C. R. (2013). Toward improved spectral measures of /s/: Results from adolescents. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 56(4), 1175-1189.
koenig2013.how: Citation confirmed on Crossref. Its /s/ peak values are known here only as quoted by Wong and Munson (2025); the paper itself was not read.

dalston1975.cite: Dalston, R. M. (1975). Acoustic characteristics of English /w, r, l/ spoken correctly by young children and adults. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 57(2), 462-469.
dalston1975.how: Citation confirmed on Crossref. Values known only as summarised by McGowan et al. (2004): F3 about 2500 Hz for /r/ and about 3500 Hz for /w/ and /l/ at 3 to 4 years. No SDs, so no band.

mcgowan2004.cite: McGowan, R. S., Nittrouer, S., and Manning, C. J. (2004). Development of [ɹ] in young, Midwestern, American children. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 115(2), 871-884.
mcgowan2004.how: Read from the PMC full text (PMC3987658). Its 2-year-old values are in figures only and come from children still acquiring /r/, so they are not used as bands.

campbell2018.cite: Campbell, H., Harel, D., Hitchcock, E., and McAllister Byun, T. (2018). Selecting an acoustic correlate for automated measurement of American English rhotic production in children. International Journal of Speech-Language Pathology, 20(6), 635-643.
campbell2018.how: Supports the choice of F3-F2 (z-scored by age and sex) as the r measure. Gives no new reference values.

nissen2005.cite: Nissen, S. L., and Fox, R. A. (2005). Acoustic and spectral characteristics of young children's fricative productions: A developmental perspective. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 118(4), 2570-2578.
nissen2005.how: Citation and abstract confirmed on Crossref. Full text behind the publisher's bot check, so no values are used.

assmann2000.cite: Assmann, P. F., and Katz, W. F. (2000). Time-varying spectral change in the vowels of children and adults. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 108(4), 1856-1866.
assmann2000.how: Citation confirmed on Crossref. Full text not reachable, so its 3, 5 and 7-year-old values are not used.

vorperian2007.cite: Vorperian, H. K., and Kent, R. D. (2007). Vowel acoustic space development in children: A synthesis of acoustic and anatomic data. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 50(6), 1510-1545.
vorperian2007.how: Read from the PMC full text (PMC2597712). Its age-by-age averages are drawn in figures only (no number tables), so no values are taken from it; it supports the notes on sex differences and age trends.

ɝ.say: F3 stays low and close to F2 through the vowel

ɚ.say: F3 stays low and close to F2 (unstressed r vowel, as in butter)

w.say: F1 and F2 both very low, F3 stays high

l.say: F3 stays high, far above F2, with sharp edges at the release; dark l has a low F2

j.say: F1 very low and F2 very high, near the i vowel

i.say: F1 low, F2 high and close to F3

eɪ.say: F1 mid, F2 high, gliding up toward i

ɛ.say: F1 mid to high, F2 fairly high

ɑ.say: F1 highest of all vowels, F2 low

oʊ.say: F1 mid, F2 low, lips rounded

u.say: F1 low, F2 low (rounded lips lower it)

ʌ.say: F1 mid to high, F2 in the middle

s.say: Loud noise high up, peak often above 6 kHz in children (much of it above what the 16 kHz copy can show)

ʃ.say: Loud noise lower than s, peak around 3 to 6 kHz in young children

spectral_peak = highest peak between 3 and 9 kHz; spectral_mean = M1. 63 children aged 2;6 to 3;6 (31 boys, 32 girls), word-initial /s/ and /ʃ/ words. gaps: Ages 0 to 59 months (under 5) for every vowel and for r: no verified table with means and SDs was reachable. Lee et al. (1999) starts at 5; Assmann and Katz (2000, ages 3, 5, 7) full text not reachable; Vorperian and Kent (2007) give these ages in figures only.

Vowels F1/F2/F3 at ages 5;0 to 9;11 and 13;0 to 17;11: Lee et al. (1999) has them by year and sex, but the raw values are behind the publisher's bot check. Only the r-vowel F3-F2 from its tokens (Flipsen et al. 2001) is in the file.

Consonant r (ɹ) F2 and F3-F2 for children: no published typical-child table with SDs found. The only child bands are F3 from children in treatment whose tokens were rated correct (McAllister Byun and Hitchcock 2012, ages 6;0 to 11;9). Intervocalic and postvocalic consonant r have no child band at all.
ɚ (unstressed r vowel, as in butter): no separate published values; only ɝ (stressed, as in bird/heard) is covered.
w, l, j in children: only Dalston's rough F3 (about 2500 vs 3500 Hz at 3 to 4 years, secondhand) and adult means (Espy-Wilson 1992). No child bands.

s and ʃ above age 3;6: Todd et al. (2011, about age 5) give means without SDs; Nissen and Fox (2005, ages 3 to 6) full text not reachable; Koenig et al. (2013, adolescents) known only secondhand. So the only s/ʃ bands are for 2;6 to 3;6.
Every other consonant (stops, nasals, f, v, θ, ð, z, ʒ, h, affricates): no age-banded spectral norms collected in this pass.

Diphthongs aɪ, aʊ, ɔɪ: Lee, Potamianos and Narayanan (2014, doi 10.1121/1.4894799) has developmental data, but its values were not read. eɪ and oʊ are covered only at their Hillenbrand steady-state point.
Peterson and Barney (1952) children: the group's ages are not documented in the data source, so it is left out.
Adult age bands (Hillenbrand men/women, Lee adults) have open upper ends; the app's children never reach them.
